Chief complaint
Rash and joint pain.

History of present illness
26-year-old woman who presents with 3 weeks of symmetric small-joint pain and swelling in the hands and wrists, morning stiffness lasting 2 hours, and a facial rash that worsens with sun exposure. She also reports mouth sores, fatigue, and 5-pound weight loss. Denies fever, chest pain, dyspnea, Raynaud phenomenon.

Past medical history
None.

Medications
Ibuprofen 600 mg TID PRN pain.

Social history
Graduate student. No tobacco. Rare alcohol.

Family history
Mother has hypothyroidism.

Review of systems
As above. Denies oral ulcers currently, alopecia, pleuritic pain.

Physical exam
Vitals: T 98.6 F, HR 88, BP 118/74, RR 14, SpO2 99% RA.
Skin: Malar erythema sparing nasolabial folds.
MSK: Swelling and tenderness of bilateral MCPs and PIPs, wrists with limited ROM.
Oral: One shallow painless ulcer on hard palate.

Objective
Labs: ANA 1:640 (H), dsDNA positive (H), C3 62 (L), C4 10 (L), ESR 48 (H), CRP 2.4 (H), Hgb 10.8 (L), WBC 3.2 (L), Plt 140 (L), Creatinine 1.3 (H), UA: protein 2+, RBC 10-20.
Urine protein/creatinine ratio: Pending.

Assessment
26-year-old woman with malar rash, inflammatory arthritis, cytopenias, and proteinuria concerning for systemic lupus erythematosus with possible lupus nephritis.

Plan
1. Systemic lupus erythematosus, new diagnosis
- Rheumatology consult
- Start hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID after eye exam
- Prednisone 40 mg daily for acute control
2. Possible lupus nephritis
- Nephrology consult; renal biopsy planning
- 24-hour urine protein when ratio returns
3. Cytopenias
- Monitor CBC; hold NSAIDs given renal involvement
